# Adapters (rendered from source)

Every side effect in the app goes through one of these seams. The app is written against the interface; the registry binds each slot to a mock, the validator, or the proof-mediated implementation. Read `lib/adapters/types.ts` for the types; this page is a rendering of it.

## Bindings

| Slot | Bound to | Chosen by |
|---|---|---|
| `persona` | env-selected (default `mock`) | `ADAPTER_PERSONA` |
| `rep` | env-selected (default `mock`; mock | validator | zk) | `ADAPTER_REP` |
| `influence` | mock (persisted through the validator state namespaces) | fixed |
| `disclosure` | mock (persisted through the validator state namespaces) | fixed |
| `mode` | mock (persisted through the validator state namespaces) | fixed |
| `rulesEngine` | mock (persisted through the validator state namespaces) | fixed |

| `graph` | mock (persisted through the validator state namespaces) | fixed |

## Which method dirties which validator namespace

The mock adapters are wrapped by `persisted()`: after a listed method runs, the named namespaces are flushed to the validator (sealed ones as ciphertext). A method not listed here writes nothing server-side.

### `disclosure` (mockDisclosureAdapter)

- setGrant → grants
- requestUnlock → unlockRequests
- respondToUnlock → unlockRequests
- followFacet → followedFacets
- unfollowFacet → followedFacets

### `mode` (mockModeAdapter)

- list → modes
- getActive → modes, activeMode
- setActive → activeMode
- create → modes
- update → modes
- duplicate → modes
- delete → modes, activeMode

### `rules` (mockRulesAdapter)

- list → rules
- create → rules
- update → rules
- delete → rules

### `attestation` (mockAttestationAdapter)

- connect → attestations
- createChannel → channels, channelMembers
- join → channelMembers
- createFolder → folders
- setFolderPublic → folders
- addToFolder → folders
- followFolder → folderFollows
- unfollowFolder → folderFollows
- openRoom → rooms
- closeRoom → rooms
- markHighlight → highlights
- pinMessage → rooms
- muteParticipant → rooms

### `identity` (mockIdentityAdapter)

- createPersona → grantsV3
- issueGrant → grantsV3
- revokeGrant → grantsV3
- requestResolution → resolutionRequests

### `graph` (mockGraphAdapter)

- addClaim → graphClaims
- setClaimActive → graphClaims
- setConsent → graphConsent, graphClaims
- startImport → imports
- advanceImport → imports
- commitImport → imports, graphClaims

### `market` (mockMarketAdapter)

- createCampaign → campaigns
- createIntent → intents, bids
- awardIntent → intents
- lapseIntent → intents

### `settle` (mockSettleAdapter)

- record → settlements
- scheduleReadwise → readwise
- rechunkReadwise → readwise
- advanceReadwise → readwise
- fastForwardAll → readwise
- sendToTimeline → sends
- setReceivePermission → receivePermission
- markCaughtUp → saturation
- clearSaturation → saturation

### EventLogAdapter

The relationship event log. Local-first: this contract is shaped so a future encrypted vault can implement it without schema change — which is why reads are all scoped to one actor and there is no cross-actor query.

| Method | Signature | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `record` | `record(event: import("@/lib/eventlog/types").EdgeEvent): Promise<import("@/lib/eventlog/types").EdgeEvent>;` | Idempotent by event id — the caller mints id + timestamp exactly once, so retrying a failed write cannot double-log. Rejects any event whose type is off the closed union (impressions are unrepresentable). |
| `list` | `list(actorPersonaId: string): Promise<import("@/lib/eventlog/types").EdgeEvent[]>;` | This actor's own log, newest first. |
| `forTarget` | `forTarget(actorPersonaId: string, targetPersona: string): Promise<import("@/lib/eventlog/types").EdgeEvent[]>;` | Events about one target, oldest first (profile history reads this). |
